audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gave Trundle zero stages in a lane he wins 56.89% of the time, and four stages disagreed with their own why-text: level 1 was 'Skill' while whys[0] says 'you win the opening exchange and set the tone'; levels 4-5 were Swain while whys[3] says 'neither kit has a clean structural advantage'; level 6 and first item were 'Skill' while whys[4] and whys[5] both hand them to Swain; 2+ items was Swain while whys[6] calls it 'genuine late-game parity'.
audit.why: Every one of those five sentences already described the right answer. The card was simply not matching the paragraph printed under it, in a matchup with a clear 167-game sample.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Trundle / Skill / Skill / Skill / Swain / Swain / Skill in both layers — identical to the packet's stage read, and now consistent with all seven why-texts.

audit.whatIsWrong: Demonic Ascension is treated as a fixed window ('fight while R is running', 'wait until his R is up') with no cooldown and no exit condition.
audit.why: Riot's text: it is a flat 120-second ultimate, and 'this form is indefinite as long as Swain drains enemy champions'. That second clause is the whole counterplay — the drain has 650 range, so walking out of it does not shorten his ultimate, it ends it. Nevermove also has a shorter cooldown while the form is up, which is why re-engaging into it feels worse than it should.
audit.corrected: The 120s cooldown, the 650 drain range, the indefinite-while-draining clause and Nevermove's reduced cooldown during the form all written into spikes[2], whys[4], mid and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nevermove is described as a pull with 'a slow cast time you can walk out of' and an 'E cast animation'. Riot's text: the wave travels out, RETURNS to Swain, and roots what it hits on the way back — the pull is a separate second cast on already-rooted targets. Vision of Empire is called a 'bomb' and a 'raven field' and never named. Chomp's sap is called attack speed in three fields.
audit.why: Dodging the outgoing wave and then standing still is exactly how players eat this root. The return leg is the dangerous half and nothing in the matchup said so.
audit.corrected: Nevermove named with its 12s rank-1 cooldown and the return-leg root stated; Vision of Empire named with its slow, reveal and Soul Fragment; Death's Hand described as stacking bolts rather than a cone; the sap corrected to attack damage.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two connected claims are wrong. mid says 'Swain has no armor or MR worth stealing through Subjugate — his stat profile is AP drain, not a tanky kit', and late invents figures: 'roughly 30-40 resistances worth of value rather than the 80-100 you strip off a Malphite'.
audit.why: Subjugate steals a percent of the target's HEALTH as well as Armor and Magic Resistance, and Ravenous Flock permanently increases Swain's maximum health every time he collects a Soul Fragment. A fragment-stacked Swain is one of the deepest health pools you will meet on a mage, so the ultimate pays — just through a different stat than the matchup assumed. The 30-40 and 80-100 figures appear nowhere in Riot's text.
audit.corrected: Rewritten around the health half of Subjugate and Ravenous Flock's permanent max-health stacking, with the invented resistance numbers removed rather than replaced.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer's TL;DR says 'anti-heal', but the content layer never mentions Grievous Wounds once across early, mid, late or any spike.
audit.why: Ravenous Flock heals him off every Soul Fragment and Demonic Ascension is a sustained drain — and Frozen Domain increases YOUR healing from all sources, so this is a pure healing race that anti-heal decides. The missing-interactions file flags Swain's Ravenous Flock sustain for this exact matchup.
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds written into mid and the level-6 discussion, tied to the moment Demonic Ascension comes online rather than as a generic buy.

edits.before: Chomp on the opening trade steals Swain's AD and Attack Speed instantly — his E pull has a slow cast time you can walk out of if you see it coming, so bully him off CS before he finds range.
edits.after: Chomp on the opening trade saps Swain's attack damage and slows him — Nevermove roots on the wave's RETURN leg, not on the way out, so keep moving after you dodge it and bully him off CS.

edits.before: Swain's Demonic Ascension goes live and flips the extended trade entirely — his sustained drain and soul fragment stacks heal through everything you output if you fight while R is running.
edits.after: Demonic Ascension (flat 120s) goes live and flips the extended trade — but the form lasts only as long as he keeps draining champions inside 650 range, so leaving the drain ends it.

edits.before: Walk out of Swain's E cast animation before the pull lands, denying the root that sets up his entire damage pattern
edits.after: Keep moving after Nevermove's wave passes you — it roots on the return leg, and the pull is a second cast on top

edits.before: Force the all-in before Level 6 while Subjugate cannot be answered by Demonic Ascension sustain
edits.after: Force the all-in before Level 6, and buy Grievous Wounds before Demonic Ascension exists

edits.before: Land E root from range and immediately pull Trundle in to eat the full W bomb detonation and Q cone burst
edits.after: Root on Nevermove's return leg, pull Trundle into Vision of Empire, then stack Death's Hand bolts

edits.before: Chomp steals his AD and AS on the first trade at Level 1 — he has no E root yet and cannot punish your walk-up, so you win the opening exchange and set the tone.
edits.after: Chomp saps his attack damage on the first trade at Level 1 — he has no Nevermove yet and cannot punish your walk-up, so you win the opening exchange and set the tone.

edits.before: E cooldown management determines who edges trades in this window — fight when his E just missed, respect his range when it is back up, and neither kit has a clean structural advantage.
edits.after: Nevermove's 12-second rank-1 cooldown decides who edges this window — fight in the beat after the return leg misses, respect his range when it is back, and neither kit has a structural edge.

edits.before: Demonic Ascension running alongside his W bomb and fragment stacks heals through your Chomp output — he controls extended fights now and forces you to spend Subjugate on a kit that offers minimal armor and MR.
edits.after: Demonic Ascension plus Vision of Empire and banked Soul Fragments heals through your Chomp output, and Nevermove's cooldown drops while the form runs — buy Grievous Wounds before this level, not after.

edits.before: Neither ultimate is a clean win condition at full build: your Subjugate payoff on an AP drain-mage is limited, and his Demonic Ascension drain can be kited or disrupted with Pillar — genuine late-game parity.
edits.after: Neither ultimate is a clean win condition at full build: Subjugate takes a percent of the max health Ravenous Flock has been stacking, and Demonic Ascension ends the moment you leave its 650 range — genuine parity.

edits.before: At Level 1 Swain has no root and you have Chomp — walk up and auto-Chomp him immediately, the AD steal and AS slow cripple his ability to trade back and your passive healing from any dying minion means you regen whatever chip he puts on you. He wants to poke with Q and wait for Level 2 when E comes online, so deny that safety by staying close enough that his Q hits you in a trade rather than free. The moment you see him wind up E, sidestep or walk behind a minion — the hand has a visible travel time and a failed pull resets his entire Level 2 combo. Reach Level 2 with a health lead and the lane is yours to bully.
edits.after: At Level 1 Swain has no root and you have Chomp — walk up and auto-Chomp him immediately. The attack-damage sap cripples his ability to trade back and King's Tribute regens whatever chip he lands off any dying minion. He wants to poke with Death's Hand and wait for Level 2 when Nevermove arrives, so deny that safety by staying close enough that his bolts cost him a trade rather than coming free. When you see the wave go out, keep moving — Nevermove roots on the RETURN leg, and a failed root resets his whole Level 2 combo. Reach Level 2 with a health lead and the lane is yours to bully.

edits.before: Levels 4 and 5 are honest — Swain now has the W bomb stacked on top of an E root that pulls you into the detonation, and his Q poke means the lane is not pure free aggression anymore. Pick your fights on his E cooldown: after a failed E pull you have roughly 12 seconds to run a Frozen Domain all-in without him having the root to stop your approach. Place Pillar behind him to cut off the retreat, stand on W ice, and cycle Chomp to stack the AD steal — in a straight melee brawl with no E available he loses. Do not fight him willingly when E is up and he has wave cover, because eating W-into-E-into-Q while low from earlier poke is where the matchup flips. At Level 6 the calculus changes hard: his Demonic Ascension sustain in an extended fight starts to genuinely compete with your Chomp regen, especially because Swain has no armor or MR worth stealing through Subjugate — his stat profile is AP drain, not a tanky kit, so your R's payoff here is smaller than against a real tank.
edits.after: Levels 4 and 5 are honest — Vision of Empire now sits on top of a Nevermove that roots on its return leg and then pulls, and Death's Hand stacks extra damage for every bolt that connects, so the lane is no longer free aggression. Pick your fights on Nevermove's 12-second rank-1 cooldown: after a failed root you have that entire window to run a Frozen Domain all-in with no root to stop your approach. Place Pillar of Ice behind him to cut the retreat, stand on your own ice, and cycle Chomp to stack the attack-damage sap — in a straight melee brawl with no root available he loses. Dodging Vision of Empire matters more than its damage suggests, because a champion it hits hands him a Soul Fragment, and Ravenous Flock turns fragments into permanent maximum health. At Level 6, buy Grievous Wounds before you fight: Demonic Ascension is a flat 120 seconds and stays up for as long as he drains champions inside its 650 range, so anti-heal and walking out are the two answers. Subjugate still pays — it takes a percent of that stacked health pool, not only his resistances.

edits.before: At first item and beyond, Swain's Liandry's or Shadowflame turns his W bomb ticks and R drain into meaningful sustained damage that your Frozen Domain healing alone cannot fully answer — and because his kit is AP-drain rather than armor/MR stacking, Subjugate gives you roughly 30-40 resistances worth of value rather than the 80-100 you strip off a Malphite. You are still the lane winner overall (56.89%) but the late edge is close and matchup-conditional: if you went Iceborn Gauntlet you have enough CDR and durability to keep Chomp cycling through his drain, and in a 5v5 teamfight his R drains whoever he targets while you can Pillar to disrupt his positioning. Win by converting early pressure to plates and drake, not by looking for the 1v1 after he has three items and a fragment stack that makes Demonic Ascension last half the fight.
edits.after: At first item and beyond, Swain's Liandry's or Shadowflame turns Vision of Empire's ticks and his drain into sustained damage that Frozen Domain healing alone cannot fully answer. Read Subjugate correctly, though: it steals a percent of health as well as armour and magic resist, and Ravenous Flock has been permanently raising his maximum health all game, so your ultimate pays through his health bar rather than through his resistances. You are still the lane winner overall (56.89%), but the late edge is close and matchup-conditional: keep Chomp cycling through his drain, walk out of the 650-range drain field to end Demonic Ascension outright rather than tanking it, and use Pillar of Ice to break his positioning in a 5v5. Win by converting early pressure into plates and drake, not by hunting the 1v1 once he has three items and a fragment stack behind him.

edits.after: At two items Subjugate takes a percent of the max health Ravenous Flock stacked all game — that is the payoff, not his resists. Parity otherwise.
